short: Silent NATO code-word spelling (M04), closed-lexicon beam search (M07) and a hand-squeeze stop (M09) are standard; one participant, and >9,000 words only offline.
position: The paper changes the letter-selection action (M04, silently attempted NATO code words), the language assistance (M07, letter beam search over a 1,152-word lexicon) and the stop command (M09, attempted hand squeeze) [@metzger2022spelling]. No prior spelling study in the curated set uses code words as a letter code (Appendix), but M04 stays standard because the evidence comes from one participant; M07 and M09 are standard because language models and hand-motor selection were already in use [@speier2016language; @pandarinath2017communication]. The claim holds for that participant and 1,152 words: median 29.41 characters per minute at 6.13% character error rate with the language model. The authors themselves set this against 90 characters per minute from attempted handwriting by a participant who could speak [@willett2021handwriting]. The overreach is "generalizable": the 9,170-word result is an offline replay, and live conversation reached 14.8% character error rate on the trials kept (§ Generalizability to larger vocabularies).
